summary: 1958 Forest Service metal cab on a rock knob in the Medicine Bow NF; cooperative, sometimes staffed in summer; reached by a 4x4 road or a walk.

facts.design: Metal flat-roof cab, about 13 by 13 feet, with a catwalk, on a rock knob; metal stairway through the boulders

access.note: About three miles of steep, rocky road; 4x4 access only, or on foot. No visitor or rental program found in these sources.

visit.trail_note: 4x4 access only, or by foot, per the register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR gives 7,885 ft (2,403 m), matching the brief's 2403.3 m; firelookout.com gives 7960 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.
The NHLR 2018 visit says staffed 'Sometimes' with seasonal USFS staff; firelookout.com says only 'Staffed.' The story uses the register's wording.

notes_for_editor: Thin on history: only three pages read and no fire or rental record found. Do not confuse with the Bighorn Mountains Black Mountain (Sheridan County, BHNF, built 1939 by the CCC, now boarded up); the Sheridan travel-history article and the Road Trip Ryan page describe that tower. Staffing dates in the register come from the 2018 visit and may have changed. Personal names of past lookouts are kept to the published lists.
